classification.difficultyReason: Relate added capacity to an extra cylindrical water depth, then add the existing depth using unrounded working.

inlines.text: A cylindrical vase is filled with water to the height shown. Sven pours in another 200 ml of water.
Calculate the new depth of the water.

spec.description: Upright open vase with elliptical opening and water surface. External arrows show water depth, full height and a centre-to-right-rim radius.
spec.mathematics: Cylinder radius 3.5 cm; initial water depth 6 cm; full height 16 cm. View from above and in front. Solid side silhouettes and front bottom arc; source does not display a rear bottom arc. Radius dimension spans the projected base centre to right rim.
spec.answerVisibility: Only 6 cm, 16 cm and 3.5 cm are labelled.

answer.worked:
Find the extra depth from $200\text{ mL}=200\text{ cm}^3$.
$$\begin{align*}V &= Ah\\200 &= \pi(3.5)^2h\\h &= \frac{200}{12.25\pi}\text{ cm}\\h &\approx5.2\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
Use the unrounded extra depth.
$$\begin{align*}\text{New depth} &= 6+\frac{200}{12.25\pi}\\\text{New depth} &\approx11.2\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
